lesson_title: The Price Rise That Lost Money
hook_text: She raised her price... and made R1 600 LESS. One number could have warned her.
clip_script: Monday, she raises voucher prices ten percent. Airtime is a need with no escape route at school: a plank. Hardly anyone stops buying, and the till total rises. Wednesday, emboldened, she raises the chocolate to thirty rand. Chocolate is a treat with escape routes everywhere: a rubber band. Sales collapse from four hundred bars to two hundred and eighty. It was twenty-five times four hundred — ten thousand rand. Now thirty times two hundred and eighty — eight thousand four hundred. She raised the price and lost one thousand six hundred rand. Plank: push price up, revenue follows. Rubber band: pull price down, revenue follows.
visual_style: A tuck shop till whose running total climbs green on Monday and bleeds red on Wednesday, with a plank and a rubber band appearing as literal props over the two products.
pacing: Two-beat structure — Monday win, Wednesday loss — with the rule delivered as a mic-drop.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to calculate elasticity and never price blind again.
